content: Atlas cache entries use a soft TTL of ninety seconds. A reader may serve the current value during that interval, while a background refresh obtains a newer value before the hard expiry.
title: Atlas refresh window

content: Atlas stale grace is separate from retry delay. After soft TTL expiry, one elected reader refreshes the entry and other readers may use the stale value for thirty seconds; after hard expiry no stale value is served.
title: Atlas stale grace rule

content: An Atlas cache key contains tenant, resource type, and stable resource identifier in that order. A deployment color is excluded so blue and green workers resolve the same logical entry.
title: Atlas cache key namespace

content: Atlas starts approximate least recently used eviction at eighty percent capacity and stops at seventy percent. Eviction changes memory pressure only; it does not alter soft TTL or hard expiry policy.
title: Atlas eviction watermark

content: Nimbus gives a consumer a forty second visibility lease. The consumer must acknowledge before the lease ends, or extend the lease while work continues; an expired lease makes the message visible again.
title: Nimbus acknowledgement lease

content: Nimbus retry delay follows fixed steps of five, twenty, and sixty seconds after consecutive failed deliveries. Visibility lease duration controls in flight ownership and is not one of the retry delay steps.
title: Nimbus retry schedule

content: Nimbus moves a message to the dead letter quarantine after four failed delivery attempts. The quarantine record keeps the original message identifier, final error class, and attempt count for inspection.
title: Nimbus quarantine threshold

content: A Nimbus producer supplies a stable deduplication token for each logical command. The broker retains the token for ten minutes and accepts a later command as new only after that retention window.
title: Nimbus duplicate suppression

content: Orchid canary deployment sends five percent of traffic for ten minutes, then twenty five percent for fifteen minutes, before full rollout. Each stage advances only when its health gate passes.
title: Orchid canary stages

content: Orchid triggers automatic rollback when the canary error ratio exceeds two percent for three consecutive one minute windows. A single brief spike records a warning but does not trigger rollback.
title: Orchid rollback gate

content: Orchid freezes configuration mutation from the start of canary traffic until rollout completion or rollback completion. Read only inspection remains available throughout the freeze.
title: Orchid configuration freeze

content: Before replacing an Orchid worker, the controller stops new assignments and allows active work to drain for up to forty five seconds. Remaining work is returned to the queue before process termination.
title: Orchid worker drain

content: Quartz verifies every sealed segment with a SHA-256 digest stored beside the segment descriptor. Recovery rejects a segment when the calculated digest differs from the descriptor digest.
title: Quartz segment verification

content: A Quartz replica independently calculates SHA-256 for each sealed segment and compares it with the descriptor value before activation. Any mismatch leaves that segment unavailable for reads.
title: Quartz replica verification

content: A Quartz read transaction binds to one immutable generation selected by the catalog pointer. Later compaction may publish another generation, but the active reader continues with its original generation until close.
title: Quartz immutable read generation

content: Quartz compaction logs may contain the labels snapshot reader version catalog isolation when describing diagnostics. Those labels are search hints only; this section defines compaction scheduling at a sixty percent fragmentation threshold.
title: Quartz compaction glossary warning

content: Zephyr keeps every trace that contains an error and samples one percent of otherwise successful traces. The decision is made at the root span and propagated to child spans.
title: Zephyr trace sampling

content: Zephyr opens a latency alert when the five minute p95 exceeds eight hundred milliseconds in three consecutive windows. One isolated slow window remains visible on the dashboard without paging.
title: Zephyr latency alert

content: Zephyr replaces customer identifiers with a deterministic one way alias before log storage. Operators can correlate events that share an alias but cannot recover the original identifier from the log entry.
title: Zephyr log redaction

content: Zephyr copies the root trace identifier into each structured event and attaches the active span identifier when available. This permits correlation between trace spans and service logs.
title: Zephyr span correlation
